turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll analyze the training data to identify patterns that lead to high yield strength and high elongation, then match candidates to those patterns.

## Step 1: Identify the Pareto Front in Training Data

From the training data, I'll identify non-dominated points (high YS AND high elongation):

Key Pareto-front observations:
- **High elongation (>50%) with moderate-high YS**: 
  - 206 MPa / 80% (Fe~70.6, Cr16, Ni9.5, Mo2, low C, HT1075/4h/air-cool, no aging)
  - 282 MPa / 65% (Fe~70.4, Cr16.6, Ni9.3, Mo1.74, HT1100/0.25h, aging 690°C/8000min)
  - 290 MPa / 78% (Fe~70.8, Cr16.4, Ni9.2, Mo1.6, HT1100/0.25h, no aging)
  - 278 MPa / 62% (Fe~71.4, Cr18, Ni8.75, Mo0, Ti0.4, HT1050/1h, 2nd HT 700°C/20h)
  - 280 MPa / 64% (Fe~54.7, Cr23.5, Ni18.5, HT1180, no aging)
  - 270 MPa / 60% (Fe~68, Cr18, Ni12, HT1075)
  - 375 MPa / 53% (Fe~62.4, Cr20.5, Ni13.5, Si2.5, HT1150)
  - 440 MPa / 50% (Fe~69.7, Cr21, Ni6, Mo2.15, HT1050)
  - 700 MPa / 34% (Fe~64.9, Cr11.25, Ni19.5, Ti2.9, HT1050, AH700)
  - 1000 MPa / 25% (Fe~60.5, Cr11.25, Ni23, Ti2.9, multi-stage AH)
  - 1300 MPa / 19% (Fe~84, Cr13, C0.2, HT1050)
  - 1380 MPa / 15% (Fe~82.95, Cr11.25, Ni1.65, W1.8, C0.13, HT1000, temper 450°C)

## Step 2: Key Composition-Process Patterns

**For high elongation + moderate YS**: 
- Austenitic stainless (Cr~16-18, Ni~8-12, low C) with solution anneal ~1050-1100°C, no aging → ~200-290 MPa, 60-80%
- Fe~70, Cr~16-18, Ni~9, Mo~1.6-2, HT at 1100°C short time → very high elongation

**For balanced trade-off**:
- Fe~62-64, Cr~11-12, Ni~19-23, Ti~2.9, AH at 700-750°C → 600-1000 MPa, 25-34%
- Fe~82-85, Cr~11-13, Ni~1.65, W~1.8, C~0.13, temper 450-550°C → 1090-1380 MPa, 13-15%

## Step 3: Match Candidates to Pareto Patterns

**c018** (Fe71.36, Cr18, Ni8.75, Ti0.4, HT1050/1h, 2nd HT 700°C/20h, aging 600°C/5000min):
- Very similar to training point 278 MPa/62% → expect ~280-310 MPa, ~55-65% elongation ✓ HIGH elongation

**c029** (Fe66.48, Cr19, Ni9, Mo1.25, Ti0.35, Nb0.35, HT1150/1.9h, AH750/24h, no aging):
- Similar to 360 MPa/38% training point (same composition, AH750/15h → 360/38%) but longer AH → expect ~350-380 MPa, ~35-40% ✓

**c056** (Fe60.47, Cr11.25, Ni23, Mo1.3, Ti2.9, Al0.4, HT1120/4h/120°C cool, AH735/16h):
- Similar to training 1000 MPa/25% (same composition, AH720/16h+640/13h) → expect ~700-900 MPa, ~25-30% ✓ HIGH strength + decent elongation

**c041** (Fe82.95, Cr11.25, Ni1.65, Mo0.425, W1.8, C0.13, HT1000/0.7h/120°C, temper 650°C/4.8h):
- Training shows same composition: temper 600°C → 910 MPa/15%, temper 550°C → 1090 MPa/15%, temper 300°C → 1330 MPa/13%
- At 650°C tempering → expect ~750-850 MPa, ~15-16% ✓ HIGH strength

**c074** (Fe60.47, Cr11.25, Ni23, Mo1.3, Ti2.9, Al0.4, HT1120/3h/120°C, AH845/4h + AH710/22.5h):
- Multi-stage AH similar to training 1000 MPa/25% pattern → expect ~900-1000 MPa, ~25% ✓ HIGH strength + moderate elongation

Let me verify these 5 span the frontier well:
- c018: ~280-310 MPa / ~60-65% (high elongation end)
- c029: ~350-380 MPa / ~35-40% (middle)
- c056: ~700-900 MPa / ~25-30% (upper middle)
- c074: ~900-1000 MPa / ~25% (high strength + moderate elongation)
- c041: ~750-850 MPa / ~15-16% (high strength end)

These 5 candidates span from high-elongation/moderate-strength to high-strength/moderate-elongation, covering the Pareto frontier well. The set is mutually non-dominated and covers the trade-off space.

Final: c018, c029, c056, c074, c041
